operatorDirective: Stop all primary-storage code changes. Bootstrap the service account, run the prover, and let actual DSM behaviour decide what else the primary needs.

rulesEncoded: Share.get establishes existence and is negatively controllable: a fabricated name returns 402, so a success is a real record rather than an echo.
Share.list is NOT an authoritative census: it omits enterprise-WORM shares, so omission alone supports no conclusion.

An ADMIN access result is not probative on a least-privilege share: FileStation returns 407 to ADMIN for the vault AND for the healthy -meta share, because both admin identities are deliberately non-writable.

enforcedInCode.interpretShareExistence: returns EXISTS when get succeeds under a holding negative control, regardless of list omission; INCONCLUSIVE when the control does not hold

closingDeliverable.whyRecorded: Each rule, misread, produces the same damage: mutating infrastructure to repair a defect that does not exist. Reading list omission as absence would have justified recreating a correctly-provisioned WORM share and discarding its UUID. Reading ADMIN 407 as unreachability would have justified changing an ACL that was already correct.

controlPreserved.role: the only known-WORM share whose WORM status does not depend on the claim under test, which is what makes Rule 1 falsifiable
controlPreserved.instruction: LEAVE UNTOUCHED until its retention state permits deliberate cleanup

backupPurchaseGateFrozen.rejectionRule: A high-capacity unit that cannot behaviourally prove immutable retention is rejected. The measured protected set is ~316 MB, so capacity is not the property being bought.
backupPurchaseGateFrozen.proofStandard: Behavioural refusal, not a datasheet claim -- the same standard applied to the primary.

operatorActionOutstanding.whyNotDoneHere: No connected Synology or Doppler control surface can perform the DSM password operation from this session, and the automation credential's user-management boundary (error 105) is being preserved by design rather than worked around.

targetGrantShape.allow: cg-context-ledger may hash an object inside the canonical immutable-context root
targetGrantShape.preferredImplementation: a forced-command wrapper rooted at the vault, which is materially stronger than adding sha256sum to a generic command allowlist

stepEAnticipated.authorityDecision: The exact grant is decided when the prover returns its concrete requirement. Nothing is broadened in advance.
